scenes.text: In the 1950s, long before he became one of the most feared crime bosses in America, a young federal inmate named James 'Whitey' Bulger volunteered for a medical study.
He was told it could help cure schizophrenia, and that volunteering might shave time off his sentence. It was actually a CIA mind-control program called MKUltra.
For roughly fifteen months, Bulger and other inmates were dosed with LSD, sometimes daily, without ever being told what the drug actually was.
He was dosed more than fifty times. Bulger later described the experience as a 'black hole of horror,' hallucinating blood pouring down the walls of his cell.
He said the nightmares from those months never fully stopped, and for the rest of his life, he believed the experiment changed something in him permanently.
Bulger wasn't the only life this program touched. The full story of MKUltra, and how much of it the CIA tried to erase, is in the pinned comment.
